knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Double Integral Over a Circle or Part-Circle Not Centered at the Origin

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y+\frac{1}{2})^{2}\leq\frac{1}{4}\}$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D y\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $\frac{1}{2}$ and center $(0,- \frac{1}{2})$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2+1y&\leq0\\r^2+1r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(- \sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq - \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Choose $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-moderate/31aaf8e1601f85ff4c8f.png)

**Transformed integrand.** The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}y&=r \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\\y\,\mathrm{d}A&=r^{2} \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2} \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3} \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor was squared instead of used once. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}r^{2} \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}}r^{3} \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor was squared instead of used once. $\displaystyle\int_{- \frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{\cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r \sin{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. The area factor is missing.

generation.domain: r>=0; tangent axis disk; once-only interior coverage

knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Double Integral Over a Circle or Part-Circle Not Centered at the Origin

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):(x+\frac{3}{2})^{2}+y^{2}\leq\frac{9}{4}\}$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $\frac{3}{2}$ and center $(- \frac{3}{2},0)$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2+3x&\leq0\\r^2+3r\cos{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(- 3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq - 3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $\frac{\pi}{2}\leq\theta\leq\frac{3 \pi}{2}$. Choose $\frac{\pi}{2}\leq\theta\leq\frac{3 \pi}{2}$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-moderate/8edfb20b8e9c0a691b38.png)

**Transformed integrand.** The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}x^{2}&=r^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\\x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A&=r^{3} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{- 3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{- 3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}}r^{4} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor was squared instead of used once.

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y-\frac{1}{2})^{2}\leq\frac{1}{4}\}$. Rewrite

\iint_D y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2-1y&\leq0\\r^2-1r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(\sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$. Choose $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$. Every interior point is covered once.

$$
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi}\int_{0}^{\sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
